subject: Urgent: Checkoutly production 502s & tokenized latency — pathchain analysis required
messages:
From: David Raines <david.r@checkoutly.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: support@checkoutly.com
Date: 2026-10-25T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: High 502 rate + token latency spike — Checkoutly production (us-west)

Kim,

We started seeing a spike in 502s and per-token latency across our checkout flow in us-west at ~07:50 PDT. Error rate rose from ~0.2% to 4.7% and median token latency jumped from ~45ms to ~320ms. The attached error sample shows repeated 502s with connection resets and some upstream TLS timeouts.

This is impacting live checkouts; we have paused a subset of campaigns but need Redwood to triage ASAP. From our side:
- Traces show increased retrying around the egress hops near our VPC peer.
- No config changes on our side in the last 12 hours.

Can you escalate to your network/runtime team? We can join a quick bridge. Execs are on standby.

Attaching: error-sample-502.json

Thanks,
David Raines
Director of Engineering, Checkoutly
Email: david.r@checkoutly.com
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: David Raines <david.r@checkoutly.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High 502 rate + token latency spike — Checkoutly production (us-west)

Thanks David — escalating.

Marissa / Ben — taking this into detective lane. Initial notes: customer reports 502 surge and token latency spike localized to us-west. They see retries clustering around egress/VPC peer boundary. I attached their error payload and asked for any immediate mitigation (routing/fallback) we can do from our side.

Ask:
- Ben, can you run a quick peering health + NAT conntrack check for Checkoutly tenant (tenant id 8234) and share any NAT exhaustion counters or proxy queue depth?
- Marissa, please surface any recent config pushes for proxies or firewall rules in us-west in the last 24h.
- If we have a recommended emergency mitigation (alternate egress route or increase proxy workers), propose it and estimate RTO/Risk.

I will set up a 12:30pm PDT bridge and loop in platform oncall if we see 10%+ sustained error rate.

Attachments: error-sample-502.json

—
Kimberly Park
Manager, Customer Escalations | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, David Raines <david.r@checkoutly.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High 502 rate + token latency spike — Checkoutly production (us-west)

Quick update from initial triage (logs and sampled path traces attached):
- Observed NAT conntrack counters for tenant 8234 approaching configured soft limit on two border nodes in us-west-2 around 07:45–08:00 PDT. This correlates with increased SYN retransmits and connection resets seen in the customer's traces.
- Proxy layer (edge-proxy-v2) shows backlog and ~3s head-of-line delay for several worker threads; this lines up with per-token latency inflation.
- DNS resolution times from our edge to the customer origin spiked briefly, but that alone doesn't explain the conntrack/503 behavior.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (risk/impact):
1) Temporarily route Checkoutly tenants on those nodes to alternate peering ports (fast, low risk) — estimate 5–10m to shift routes, no deploy.
2) Increase proxy worker pool for affected edge-proxy instances (moderate risk, requires config push and warm-up — ~20m).
3) Raise NAT conntrack soft limits for the two nodes as emergency relief (higher risk for other tenants on same nodes — ~10m).

I recommend option 1 + 2 in parallel. I'll prepare the routing change and a short playbook. Attaching path-trace-20261025.txt and sla-impact-summary.pdf with sample counters.

Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Exec heads-up: Checkoutly outage window and customer sync at 12:30 PT

Team — fyi, I've briefed our GTM execs. Checkoutly has asked for an exec-level sync at 12:30 PT to review impact and remediation posture. They are sensitive given peak traffic hours.

Please have a short runbook in the meeting: what we've observed, immediate mitigation applied, rollback plan (if any), and expected customer-facing ETA to return to baseline. Also be prepared to answer whether this was caused by an internal config change vs external transit anomaly.

If Ben's plan (route shift + increase workers) is ready, we'll execute and confirm before the customer call. I can join the bridge and own the executive communication.

—
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Incident Response | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: David Raines <david.r@checkoutly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: High 502 rate + token latency spike — Checkoutly production (us-west)

David,

Thanks for the patience. Summary of actions taken so far and next steps:
- 10:55 PDT: Applied emergency route shift for tenant 8234 away from the two impacted peering ports (option 1). Initial telemetry shows error rate dropping from 4.7% -> 1.1% and median token latency reduced to ~110ms.
- 11:10 PDT: Increased proxy worker pool on affected edge-proxy instances (option 2). We saw further steadying of latency and reduction in backlog.
- Ben flagged NAT conntrack approaching soft limits — we'll schedule a safe, capacity-aware conntrack limit increase on the two nodes later tonight as a durable fix after verifying cross-tenant risk.

We're holding a 12:30 PT bridge to walk through the above and confirm customer observations. Please join: https://meetings.example.com/checkoutly-sync-20261025

Requested from Checkoutly: any additional traces or failing sample requests you can share prior to the call.

We will follow up after the bridge with a short RCA timeline and permanent remediation plan.

Attachments: path-trace-20261025.txt, sla-impact-summary.pdf

Best,
Kimberly Park
Manager, Customer Escalations | Redwood Inference
